village.title: Village of Oak Park — Traffic Crash Dashboard
village.description: Every crash on a public roadway inside the Village reported to the Oak Park Police Department since 1 Jan 2024, from the Power BI model behind the Village dashboard. Posted about a week after each crash.

idot.title: Illinois Department of Transportation — statewide crash data
idot.description: IDOT’s annual crash files (one ArcGIS layer per year), filtered to crashes IDOT locates in Oak Park. Covers every reporting agency, including Illinois State Police on I-290, but only state-reportable crashes: an injury or death, or property damage over $1,500 ($500 if a vehicle is uninsured; 625 ILCS 5/11-407).

osm.title: OpenStreetMap — basemap streets, rail, parks and boundary
osm.description: Street, rail, park and Village-boundary geometry from OpenStreetMap (via the Overpass API), baked into a static file. © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License.

method: Raw tables are fetched verbatim (data/raw/), then decoded and normalized by extract/build.ts. Village crash counts are re-derived from the raw rows and checked against the Village dashboard’s own published totals for every year and severity; the build fails on any mismatch. Weather, lighting, road-surface and traffic-control codes are decoded with tables derived from IDOT’s own rows, which publish each code beside its label. A crash’s severity is its most severe injury on the KABCO scale (K fatal, A incapacitating, B non-incapacitating, C possible injury, O none). “KSI” means killed or seriously injured (K + A).
known_issues: The two sources count different things and are never added together. Village data: every Oak Park PD report since 2024, including minor crashes, but not crashes worked by the State Police on I-290. IDOT data: all agencies including I-290, but only crashes above IDOT’s reporting threshold, and finalized months after year-end.
Counts are crashes, not people: a crash that injured three people counts once in crash totals. People-injured totals (K/A/B/C counts) are shown separately where labelled.

“Pedestrian” and “bicycle” crashes are classified by the crash’s first harmful event (IDOT “Type of First Crash”). A crash that began as a collision between vehicles and then struck a pedestrian is counted as a vehicle crash.
17 of 4939 Village crashes have no usable coordinates and are left off the map (they still count in every total).
156 of 17098 IDOT crashes have no usable coordinates.
IDOT’s 2014–2017 files record longitude without its minus sign (6165 crashes); the sign is restored here.
2 separate Village crashes (different times and places) share a police report number. They are counted as separate crashes, as the Village dashboard also does.
1 IDOT row(s) are misaligned in IDOT’s own file (fields shifted by a stray comma); their severity is shown as “Unknown”.
IDOT leaves the investigating agency blank for: 2025 (1369 crashes). Interstate crashes are identified by road class (IDOT functional class “InterState”), which is populated for every year.
The newest IDOT year may still be preliminary; IDOT revises recent files as late reports arrive.
The Village posts crashes about a week after they occur, so the most recent days are incomplete.
